hints.title: Chronological Simultaneous Secret Sharing Obstacle
hints.text: Secret propagation happens instantaneously during concurrent meetings at the same timestamp. If a participant has no connection to someone with the secret at that exact time, the temporary connection must be undone. How can chronological grouping maintain valid state?

hints.title: Batch Connected Reset Invariant
hints.text: Meetings at identical timestamps can share information transitively among participants. If a component does not connect to the secret source during that time step, their connections must be rolled back.

hints.title: Timestamp Grouped Disjoint Set Rollback Procedure
hints.text: Initially union person 0 with firstPerson. Sort meetings by timestamp and group concurrent meetings together. For each time step, union participants in that time group. Afterward, inspect every participant involved in the batch: if their canonical root differs from the root of person 0, reset their parent pointer to themselves. Finally, return all individuals sharing the root of person 0.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Sorting meetings takes O(M log M); processing each meeting and resetting unconnected nodes takes near-linear time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Naive global BFS across all time intervals fails because information cannot travel backward in time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Grouping meetings by timestamp requires O(M) additional memory; parent array uses O(N).
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Resetting disjoint set parent pointers for batch participants who did not reach root 0.

solutions.approach: Timestamp-grouped disjoint set union with un-union reset for uninfected participants
